# Languages

The plan that built this was `docs/next-i18n.md`, deleted once its last phase shipped; its research,
decisions and measurements stay in git (`git show 3dc0080:docs/next-i18n.md`). This file holds the
rules; `docs/i18n-glossary.md` the words and their sources; `docs/autocad-coverage.md` what each
language's command line does and what `ar` still needs to go live.

## Two languages, two catalogs

- **The interface language** is the URL's (`/`, `/es`, `/ar`). **The command language** is the
  engine's: command names and aliases, prompts, keywords, command-line messages and everything drawn
  on the canvas. `en` and `ar` use the global commands, `es` Spanish AutoCAD's (brief §4).
- **The app's texts are in `messages/<locale>.json`** (next-intl); **the engine's in
  `cad/locales/`** (`cad-engine.instructions.md`). What the engine names — snaps, entity types,
  tools, colours, ByLayer, a command's aliases, the preset views, the ViewCube's faces and compass
  letters — the host reads from the engine
  (`EngineState.names`, `state.tools`, `engineText()`), never copies into `messages/`.
- The engine's language contract for any host — the entry points, what a language may leave out,
  compiling its messages, `extendLocale`, `EngineNames` — is `cad/README.md`. This app is held to
  it like any host: `@/cad` and `@/cad/locales/<tag>` only (`cad/entryPoints.test.ts`).
- English is the source and the type: `AppConfig.Messages` is `typeof en`, and
  `createMessagesDeclaration` types every argument from `messages/en.json`. The declaration,
  `messages/en.d.json.ts`, is generated by `next typegen` (part of `npm run typecheck`) and
  ignored by git. `tsc` runs with `--incremental false`: the incremental cache does not notice a
  change in that declaration and keeps reporting — or hiding — stale argument errors.

## URLs without a proxy

- `i18n/routing.ts` is the only list of languages, with `DIRECTION`, `LOCALE_STATUS` and
  `OG_LOCALE`. English has no prefix (`as-needed`), the others do; slugs are never translated.
- `i18n/rewrites.ts` builds the whole scheme, and `i18n/rewrites.test.ts` fixes it with Next's own
  matcher: redirects (`/en/…` → `/…`), `afterFiles` rewrites (English paths onto `/en/…`, after
  the files and before `[locale]`), and `fallback` rewrites (any unknown path of a language onto
  that language's 404). There is no `proxy.ts`: it would run a function on every visit to a
  static site. Add one only if the language ever has to be negotiated.
- **Every site link is `localePath(locale, href)`** or `sitePaths()` (`i18n/navigation.ts`), which a
  test holds equal to next-intl's `getPathname`. Never import `next-intl/navigation` into the app:
  `createNavigation` registers its client `Link` wherever it is imported, putting next-intl's client
  runtime (~12 KB gz) on the landing, and its `Link` with a `locale` prefixes `/en`, a redirect.
- `[locale]` is a root param. Both root layouts export `generateStaticParams` over
  `routing.locales` and `dynamicParams = false`; `i18n/request.ts` reads `next/root-params`, and
  nothing calls `setRequestLocale`. Route handlers cannot read root params: they take `params` and
  name the locale (`getTranslations({ locale, namespace })`), as `global-not-found.tsx` names the
  default one. No metadata files (`opengraph-image`, `manifest`) inside `[locale]` — they would give
  English an `/en/…` URL; the OG images and manifests are named route handlers.
- **A language's 404** is `[locale]/(marketing)/404/page.tsx` calling `notFound()`, prerendered and
  reached through the `fallback` rewrite, rendered by `(marketing)/not-found.tsx` inside the
  layout. Never a `[...rest]` catch-all: it is rendered on demand, a function per mistyped URL. Next
  16.3 sends a page's `notFound()` as an empty document with the 404 status and the metadata and
  draws it in the browser — the catch-all does the same. `global-not-found.tsx` is left for what
  never reaches a language (`/404` itself).

## Messages

- Keys are semantic (`Editor.CommandBar.save`), never the English sentence.
- **ICU, fully.** A number argument is `{count, number}` — next-intl types a bare `{count}` as a
  string. A count that changes the words is `{count, plural, one {…} other {…}}`, never a pair of
  keys; every plural has `other`. A link or an emphasis inside a sentence is a rich tag read with
  `t.rich`. Messages are precompiled at build time (`experimental.messages.precompile`), so the
  browser gets icu-minify's formatter and never a parser, and **`t.raw()` is off limits** (a
  precompiled message with arguments is an array, not its source).
- `loadMessages` lays a language over English key by key, so a missing key shows English, never
  the key. `mergeMessages` treats a precompiled array as a leaf.
- **A count is a plural wherever the language's words agree with it.** Arabic's noun changes with
  the number (`عنصر واحد`, `عنصران`, `3 عناصر`, `11 عنصرًا`, `100 عنصر`), so its messages use
  the six categories where English prints a bare `{n, number}`; the test takes a plural and a
  number as the same argument type. `other` is always there.
- `i18n/messages.test.ts`: every catalog parses, plurals have `other`, a translation has only
  English's keys with English's arguments and tags, and a `live` or finished language has all of
  them (`TRANSLATED`).
- Command names inside prose (`Type a command (LINE, TR, CO…)`) are written in the command language
  of that locale — `LINEA`, `DF`, `ESCALATL` in Spanish, the global ones in Arabic. So is a line
  that belongs to the command line, such as the 404's `Pulse F1 para obtener ayuda.`
- **Scripts are portable**: a figure's script names each command by its global name with `_`
  (`.command("_OFFSET")`), as an AutoCAD script written for every language does, and keywords by
  id (`.option("Close")`). The transcript shows each command as its language names it, and the
  hero times the name shown. Code that looks for a command's line asks the engine for its name
  (`engineText(locale).commandNames("OFFSET")`).

## Left-to-right runs in right-to-left text

- A command name, a key, a value with its unit, an address or a URL inside Arabic text is isolated
  with FSI…PDI (U+2068…U+2069), written in the catalog as the JSON escapes `\u2068` and `\u2069`
  so a translator sees them. Not a rich tag: a tag has to exist in English too (the catalog test),
  and would turn a dozen string props into nodes. The isolates do the same in HTML, attributes,
  metadata, the manifest and the share card (`lib/og.tsx` drops them before Satori).
- A name pasted from that prose into the command line still runs: `setCommandLineText` drops bidi
  controls.
- What is in the command language is marked up as such: `lang={state.commandLine.lang}` (or
  `engineText(locale).commandTag` on the server) on its lines — transcripts, the command line, the
  dynamic input, the 404's line — and the command board's key caps and lists are LTR islands. Not on
  a container whose `aria-label` is in the page's language.

## Writing Spanish

- Terms are Autodesk's Spanish ones (`docs/i18n-glossary.md`, with its sources): referencia a
  objetos, rastreo polar, Modo Forzcursor, cinta de opciones, PorCapa, Definir actual…
- The landing says tú («Escribe L. Pulsa Intro. Dibuja.»); the editor keeps Autodesk's register:
  labels are infinitives and nouns («Guardar dibujo»), sentences say usted («Escriba un comando»).
- Neutral Spanish: no vosotros or voseo, «equipo» or «dispositivo» (not ordenador or computadora),
  «archivo» (not fichero), «Intro» for the Enter key and «Supr» for Delete, as Autodesk's help
  writes them. Angle quotes «» in prose, and em dashes attached to the aside: «cotas —lineal…—».
- Search texts are written from what Spanish speakers search (`docs/i18n-glossary.md`, "Search
  texts"), not translated: «CAD 2D online gratis», «comandos de AutoCAD», «sin registro».

## Writing Arabic

- Modern Standard Arabic, neutral across the region, with `docs/i18n-glossary.md`. There is no
  Arabic AutoCAD to copy, so each term says how it was chosen there, and a native speaker reviews
  every batch before it is `live`.
- The landing speaks in the imperative («اكتب L. اضغط Enter. ارسم.»); the editor labels with verbal
  nouns («حفظ الرسم»). «أوتوكاد» in prose, AutoCAD only in the trademark notice.
- Arabic punctuation (، ؛ ؟), «» in prose, latin digits; a list is `format.list` (`LINE وCIRCLE`).
  An arrow that points along the reading direction is `←`.
- Command names inside prose are the global ones (Arabic's command language), and so is a line
  of the command line such as the 404's `Press F1 for help.`
- Search texts come from what Arabic speakers search (`docs/i18n-glossary.md`, "Search texts"):
  «رسم هندسي», «ثنائي الأبعاد», «أون لاين», «مجاني», «أوامر أوتوكاد واختصاراتها». «كاد» alone is
  useless.

## Fonts per script

- Inter and Geist Mono are latin only. A script they lack gets a face on its own pages only:
  `scriptFontVariables` (`lib/fonts.ts`) overrides `--font-sans` and `--font-mono` on `<html>`
  with the face right behind Inter or Geist Mono and **before either fallback** — a fallback is a
  local Arial, which has Arabic and would take those letters first. The face is declared in both
  root layouts with `preload: false`: a preload in a shared layout would fetch it on every page.
  `/` and `/es` never name Readex Pro, so they never download it.
- Arabic is Readex Pro, variable, `subsets: ["arabic"]`: 23 KB of woff2 (27/09/2026), against 31
  for Cairo or Alexandria, 89 for IBM Plex Sans Arabic in two weights (which also breaks Satori's
  parser) and 166 for Noto Sans Arabic. A new script's face is weighed the same way.
- `:lang(ar)` (both stylesheets, unlayered so it outranks the utilities): no tracking, capitals
  or italics; the landing's running text at 1.8, headlines at 1.3 and calibrated display sizes;
  Arabic in `label-mono`/`data-mono` on the sans stack (Geist Mono lent it 0.6 em spaces), except
  inside an LTR island. Select by attributes, never `:dir()`: Lightning CSS lowers it to a list of
  `:lang()` that matches inside the islands too.

## The engine's language

- `loadEngineLocale(locale)` (`i18n/engine.ts`) maps a page language to its engine catalog, one
  dynamic import apiece; English is built in. The editor's page loads it on the server and hands it
  to `CadWorkspace`, so the engine starts in its language without another request; the live sketch
  loads it with the engine, on intent.
- **The landing's build draws in the page's language**: `pageEngineLocale()` (`lib/plot.ts`) for
  `renderFigure`, `plotDemo`, `commandCatalog`/`autocadCommands` and `engineText(locale)` — never
  `engineText()` bare, which is English. A figure with words of its own (the two diagrams) is built
  from messages (`DIAGRAMS` in `content/figures.ts`), and centres a label with TEXT justified `MC`;
  TEXT keeps the last justification, as AutoCAD's TEXTJUSTIFY does, so a left-aligned label comes
  first.

## Where messages reach the browser

- **The landing never wraps its tree in `NextIntlClientProvider`.** An island takes its copy as
  props. A count it formats itself arrives as `pluralMessage(locale, (count) => t(key, { count }))`,
  one form per plural category of the language, and is formatted with `formatPlural()`
  (`lib/plural.ts`) — `Intl.PluralRules` and `Intl.NumberFormat` of that locale, no ICU runtime. A
  template with a slot the server cannot fill (the typed command of the 404, of the try-it box)
  comes from the engine with a placeholder name and is filled in the island.
- **The editor gets `Editor.*` and nothing else**: its layout passes `messages={{ Editor: … }}`,
  because without `messages` the provider ships every message of the site. Components in
  `components/cad/` read `useTranslations("Editor.<Part>")`, which a test enforces.
- `Intl` always gets the page's locale (`getLocale()`, `getFormatter()`), never a literal `"en"`.

## No literals

`react/jsx-no-literals` covers `components/cad/**` and `components/marketing/**`, allowing only
signs and notation the same in every language (`×`, `—`, `·`, `°`, the axis names `X` and `Y`, and
the `→` that `ForwardArrow` mirrors). **It does not see attributes** —
`aria-label`, `title`, `placeholder`, a `label` prop — so those are held to the same rule by review.
Data that is not language (a drawing number, a scale) is a named constant.

## Draft and live

- `LOCALE_STATUS` decides. A `draft` language is built and reachable, `noindex`, and absent from the
  `hreflang` set, the sitemap and the language selector. `languageAlternates()` emits `hreflang`
  (every live language plus `x-default`) only once two are live.
- **The language selector is `LanguageLinks`** (`components/language-links.tsx`): the page being
  read in every live language, as plain `<a href hrefLang lang>` links named in their own language
  (`LANGUAGE_NAMES`, never a flag) — crawlable, and a full page load, since `lang`, `dir`, the fonts
  and the engine's catalog all change. It reads the path with `usePathname` and drops the language
  (`unlocalizedPath`), which gives the same links on the server, where a prerender sees
  `/en/privacy`, and in the browser, which shows `/privacy`. It sits in the landing's footer and
  bar and in the editor's About panel; the autosave has no language, so the drawing survives a
  switch.
- Each page's canonical, `og:locale`, JSON-LD `inLanguage`/`url`, manifest and share card are its
  language's (`pageMetadata`, `lib/structured-data.ts`, `app/[locale]/og`, `…/manifest.webmanifest`).
- `<html lang dir>` comes from the locale in both root layouts, and `DirectionProvider`
  (`components/ui/direction.tsx`) is mounted with the same direction. In RTL the shell mirrors
  and the drawing, the command language and every technical value do not (`ui.instructions.md`,
  `marketing.instructions.md`); `ar` is written and stays `draft` until a native speaker has
  reviewed it — what is left before it goes `live` is listed under "Arabic interface" in
  `docs/autocad-coverage.md`.
- **What the engine draws is tagged with the command language** (`Scene.lang`, set by both
  presenters): a page's `lang` picks the font of a generic family, and an Arabic page's
  `monospace` drew the UCS icon's letters in another face.

## Budgets

What languages may add, gzip -9 unless it says Brotli; each was measured on a production build,
and a change near one measures again against the build before it:

| What                                              | Budget                             | Measured                  |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| The English engine catalog, in the engine's chunk | ≤ 8 KB                             | 6.7 KB (01/10/2026)       |
| Another language's engine catalog (own chunk)     | ≤ 12 KB                            | `es` 7.3 KB, `ar` 3.3 KB  |
| `Editor.*` in the editor's HTML                   | the editor's messages only         | 2.1 KB in English         |
| next-intl's runtime in the editor                 | precompiled messages               | 5.4 KB (11.8 uncompiled)  |
| A language's first load of the landing, Brotli    | ≤ 250 KB; 275 with a script's font | `/` 231.9, `/ar` 255.8 KB |
| Functions per page visit                          | none: no proxy, all `○` or `●`     | none                      |

The landing's own JS and fonts are in `marketing.instructions.md`; the editor's chunk is not a
budget.

## Adding a language

1. `i18n/routing.ts`: `locales`, `DIRECTION`, `LOCALE_STATUS` (`draft`), `OG_LOCALE`.
2. `messages/<locale>.json` and its entry in `catalogs` (`i18n/messages.ts`); once it is written in
   full, add it to `TRANSLATED` in `i18n/messages.test.ts`.
3. The engine's catalog, `cad/locales/<locale>.json` (`cad-engine.instructions.md`), and its entry
   in `i18n/engine.ts`.
4. Its words in `docs/i18n-glossary.md`, with their sources.
5. A script Inter lacks: its face in both root layouts (`preload: false`), `scriptFontVariables`,
   its `:lang()` rules, and a whole face for the share card if Satori is to draw it.
6. `npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `test`; a production build shows the new pages as `●`, never `ƒ`;
   screenshots of the landing at 360 px and of the editor's palettes, for text that no longer fits.
7. Going `live` adds it to the selector, `hreflang` and the sitemap — and every English key must
   exist. A language without an AutoCAD of its own goes live only after a native speaker's review,
   and its announcement leaves the Status section's «Next up» in every language in the same commit.
